messages.content:
Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a document titled `Owen — sanitized campaign snapshot performance entry` in the `People` folder. Date the entry to the completed snapshot run and write a concise, evidence-based performance note covering Owen’s execution, the inventory denominator, status-and-owner completeness, the independent owner-change validation, and the scope of my review. Keep the distinction between preparation, validation, and review explicit.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Owen — sanitized campaign snapshot performance entry", "folder": "People", "body": "Date of completed snapshot run: December 3, 2027

Performance note

Preparation — Owen completed the December sanitized campaign snapshot after the delayed owner certification arrived with its required source and through-date intact. He preserved the certification delay in the closure-and-exception summary, did not substitute stale data, and completed the run through the documented routine process.

Inventory and completeness — The snapshot used the documented sanitized campaign inventory denominator. The run record does not state a new numeric campaign count, so this entry does not infer one. Required fields, including status-and-owner coverage, were complete, named-owner certification was present, and established definitions were unchanged.

Validation — Independent owner-change validation remained in the designated owner lane and was completed without an unresolved cross-surface discrepancy. This validation was separate from Owen’s preparation and source-completeness work; no semantic dispute emerged.

Review — Riley’s review was limited to the certification-delay exception when the snapshot opened visibly Incomplete. Riley did not replace Owen’s preparation or routine closure responsibility. After the certified input arrived, Owen completed the routine closure and issued the normal summary.

Overall assessment — Owen executed the preparation and completion workflow with disciplined incomplete-state handling, explicit denominator treatment, complete status-and-owner fields, and preserved separation between preparation, independent validation, and Riley’s bounded exception review. This entry records routine source-completeness execution only; it does not grant Owen board-readiness, causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language authority."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_176_03", "path": "args", "criterion": "The performance entry is dated July 2, 2026 and states that Owen independently completed the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot on the established second-business-day cadence after taking over preparation. Missing or contradicting the date, independence, completion, or cadence must fail.

The entry states that the completed snapshot contained 135 unique campaigns and that every campaign had both a current-or-archived status and an assigned owner. Any different denominator or incomplete coverage must fail.

The entry states that Ines independently checked two owner changes against the underlying lifecycle records and verified both. Missing the validator, the count, the underlying-record check, or the successful result must fail.

The entry clearly distinguishes Riley's role from Owen's preparation and Ines's validation by stating that Riley reviewed only Owen's exception summary and did not reconcile the snapshot line by line. Any claim that Riley performed the preparation, owner-change validation, or line-by-line reconciliation must fail.", "value": {"title": "Owen — sanitized campaign snapshot performance entry", "folder": "People", "body": "Date of completed snapshot run: December 3, 2027

Performance note

Preparation — Owen completed the December sanitized campaign snapshot after the delayed owner certification arrived with its required source and through-date intact. He preserved the certification delay in the closure-and-exception summary, did not substitute stale data, and completed the run through the documented routine process.

Inventory and completeness — The snapshot used the documented sanitized campaign inventory denominator. The run record does not state a new numeric campaign count, so this entry does not infer one. Required fields, including status-and-owner coverage, were complete, named-owner certification was present, and established definitions were unchanged.

Validation — Independent owner-change validation remained in the designated owner lane and was completed without an unresolved cross-surface discrepancy. This validation was separate from Owen’s preparation and source-completeness work; no semantic dispute emerged.

Review — Riley’s review was limited to the certification-delay exception when the snapshot opened visibly Incomplete. Riley did not replace Owen’s preparation or routine closure responsibility. After the certified input arrived, Owen completed the routine closure and issued the normal summary.

Overall assessment — Owen executed the preparation and completion workflow with disciplined incomplete-state handling, explicit denominator treatment, complete status-and-owner fields, and preserved separation between preparation, independent validation, and Riley’s bounded exception review. This entry records routine source-completeness execution only; it does not grant Owen board-readiness, causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language authority."}}]}

{"results":[{"check_id":"riley_176_03","passed":false,"reason":"The body contradicts the required date by stating “December 3, 2027,” not July 2, 2026. It also omits the established second-business-day cadence and Owen’s independent takeover of preparation; explicitly declines to state the required denominator of 135 unique campaigns; does not identify Ines, two owner changes, checks against underlying lifecycle records, or verification of both; and says Riley reviewed a “certification-delay exception,” not only Owen’s exception summary, without stating that Riley did not reconcile the snapshot line by line."}]}
